summary.tagline: The Ring of Kerry (Irish: Mórchuaird Chiarraí) is a 179-kilometre-long (111-mile) circular tourist route in Co

days.title: Heritage and Forts of the North
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Cahergall
stops.detail: Apart from the coastal landscape and the region around Killarney, the restored stone forts of Cahergall, Leacanabuaile (near Cahersiveen) and Staigue Fort are particularly worth seeing.

stops.name: Heritage Center
stops.detail: In Caherciveen there is the Heritage Center with a museum in a former British fort.

stops.name: Kerry Bog Village
stops.detail: The open-air museum Kerry Bog Village is located between the towns of Killorglin and Glenbeigh.

days.title: National Park Views and Valleys
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Ladies’ View
stops.detail: Located on the Ring of Kerry, among others, is Ladies' View, a viewpoint with a view of the Upper Lake of Killarney National Park.

stops.name: Black Valley
stops.detail: In addition to the motorway, which is heavily used in high season, there is both a Ring of Kerry hiking trail, which follows a different route, and a cycle path through the Black Valley, which leads via quiet paths.

stops.name: Kerry Woollen Mills
stops.detail: The Kerry Woollen Mills are witnesses to the textile industry.

days.title: Island and Coastal Excursions
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Valentia Island
stops.detail: On St. Finian's Bay and on Valentia Island, additional secondary routes are signposted, about 40 km long, which are not included in the official part of the route, but are just as interesting and, above all, lonelier.

stops.name: Skellig Michael
stops.detail: An excursion to Skellig Michael can also be recommended.
